name: Graham Little-Piccardi-Lassueur syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of follicular lichen planopilaris causing scarring alopecia of the scalp
Non-scarring alopecia of axillary and pubic hair
Follicular keratotic papules on the trunk and extremities
Histopathological confirmation showing lichenoid interface dermatitis with perifollicular fibrosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (scarring scalp alopecia, non-scarring axillary/pubic alopecia, and follicular keratotic papules) must be present for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical triad is evident

imaging: Dermoscopy showing follicular plugging and perifollicular erythema
other: Histopathology: lichenoid interface dermatitis with perifollicular fibrosis and lymphocytic infiltrate

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of non-scarring axillary and pubic alopecia
Lack of follicular keratotic papules on trunk
Characteristic discoid plaques with central scarring

redFlags: Rapid progression of scalp scarring alopecia
Signs of secondary infection or ulceration
references: Graham Little syndrome: a rare variant of lichen planopilaris. Dermatol Clin. 2015;33(1):123-129.
Orphanet: Graham Little-Piccardi-Lassueur syndrome. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2020.
Lichen planopilaris and Graham Little syndrome: clinical and histopathological features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018;78(3):567-574.
